scenes.section: When can people join or leave?

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Open enrollment**. What it is: A yearly window to join, leave or switch plans. Changes usually start on the first day of the new plan year. Example: Emily's employer holds it each November for cover starting 1 January. The ACA Marketplace runs roughly November to mid-January in most states. Medicare's runs 15 October to 7 December.
lines.say: Open enrollment. What it is: A yearly window to join, leave or switch plans. Changes usually start on the first day of the new plan year. Example: Emily's employer holds it each November for cover starting 1 January. The A C A Marketplace runs roughly November to mid-January in most states. Medicare's runs 15 October to 7 December.

lines.raw: **Special enrollment** (after a QLE). What it is: A short window, usually **30 days** for employer plans and **60 days** for the Marketplace, after a life event. Example: Daniel losing his job and his cover.
lines.say: Special enrollment (after a Q L E). What it is: A short window, usually 30 days for employer plans and 60 days for the Marketplace, after a life event. Example: Daniel losing his job and his cover.

lines.raw: **New hire**. What it is: A new employee can join when they start, sometimes after a short waiting period. Example: Emily joining her company, cover from 1 Jan 2022.
lines.say: New hire. What it is: A new employee can join when they start, sometimes after a short waiting period. Example: Emily joining her company, cover from 1 Jan 2022.

lines.raw: Common qualifying life events (QLEs).

lines.raw: **Marriage**. Typical change: Add the new spouse (and their children).
lines.say: Marriage. Typical change: Add the new spouse (and their children).

lines.raw: **Birth or adoption**. Typical change: Add the baby; cover can start from the **date of birth** or adoption.
lines.say: Birth or adoption. Typical change: Add the baby; cover can start from the date of birth or adoption.

lines.raw: **Loss of other cover**. Typical change: Add a family member who lost their own job-based cover, like Daniel.
lines.say: Loss of other cover. Typical change: Add a family member who lost their own job-based cover, like Daniel.

lines.raw: **Divorce**. Typical change: Remove the former spouse.
lines.say: Divorce. Typical change: Remove the former spouse.

lines.raw: **Child turns 26**. Typical change: Child's dependent cover ends.
lines.say: Child turns 26. Typical change: Child's dependent cover ends.

scenes.section: COBRA: keeping cover after leaving a job

lines.raw: **COBRA** is a US law that lets people who leave a job (and their families) **keep the same employer plan for a while**, usually up to **18 months**.
lines.say: COBRA is a U S law that lets people who leave a job (and their families) keep the same employer plan for a while, usually up to 18 months.

lines.raw: It applies to employers with **20 or more employees**.
lines.say: It applies to employers with 20 or more employees.

lines.raw: The catch: the person pays the **full premium**, both their share and the employer's, plus up to 2% for admin.
lines.say: The catch: the person pays the full premium, both their share and the employer's, plus up to 2 percent for admin.

lines.raw: That is why Daniel chose Emily's plan instead.
lines.say: That is why Daniel chose Emily's plan instead.

scenes.section: COBRA: keeping cover after leaving a job

lines.raw: COBRA in the data.
lines.say: COBRA in the data.

lines.raw: A COBRA member keeps a span on the old employer's plan, often flagged as COBRA or with a special coverage code.
lines.say: A COBRA member keeps a span on the old employer's plan, often flagged as COBRA or with a special coverage code.

lines.raw: A person has **up to 60 days** to choose COBRA, and if they do, cover is backdated to the day the old cover ended.
lines.say: A person has up to 60 days to choose COBRA, and if they do, cover is backdated to the day the old cover ended.

lines.raw: So a span can appear **after** the dates it covers.
lines.say: So a span can appear after the dates it covers.

lines.raw: Retroactive changes.
lines.say: Retroactive changes.

lines.raw: Eligibility is often updated **late**.
lines.say: Eligibility is often updated late.

lines.raw: An employer may tell the insurer on 20 May that an employee left on 31 March.
lines.say: An employer may tell the insurer on 20 May that an employee left on 31 March.

lines.raw: The insurer then sets a **retroactive termination** ("retro term"): the term date is moved back to 31 March.
lines.say: The insurer then sets a retroactive termination ("retro term"): the term date is moved back to 31 March.

lines.raw: Claims already paid for April and May for that person may now be **outside** their cover.
lines.say: Claims already paid for April and May for that person may now be outside their cover.

lines.raw: The insurer may reverse them and recover the money (the Medical course explains claim reversals).
lines.say: The insurer may reverse them and recover the money (the Medical course explains claim reversals).

lines.raw: Retro changes can also go the other way: a **retro add**, like a baby born on 10 January whose parents report the birth on 25 January: cover is backdated to the birth date.
lines.say: Retro changes can also go the other way: a retro add, like a baby born on 10 January whose parents report the birth on 25 January: cover is backdated to the birth date.

lines.raw: US rules (the ACA) **limit** when cover can be cancelled backwards, so insurers follow strict policies for retro terms.
lines.say: U S rules (the A C A) limit when cover can be cancelled backwards, so insurers follow strict policies for retro terms.
